paraphrase: O Acyuta, with body like an emerald mountain, coral lips and red lotus eyes, chief of the immortals, darling of the cowherds — rather than lose the sweetness of saying these names, I would not want the sweetness of ruling Indra's world, O Lord of the great city of Araṅgam.
speaker: Toṇṭaraṭippoṭi Āḻvār
notes: 'paccai mā malai pōl mēṉi ... accuvai peṟiṉum vēṇṭēṉ'.

paraphrase: I have given up the brahminhood of bathing and tending the three fires; I have no fitting knowledge or conduct; I have nothing — O Lord of Araṅgam, you alone are my refuge.
speaker: Toṇṭaraṭippoṭi Āḻvār

paraphrase: Your devotees, even if born of the lowest, are to be honoured as you are; but brāhmaṇas of the highest birth who have learned the six limbs and the four Vedas, if they revile your devotees, become at that very moment outcastes.
speaker: Toṇṭaraṭippoṭi Āḻvār
